newsitem.title: UK: European precious metals lifeless ahead of weekend.
newsitem.headline: European precious metals lifeless ahead of weekend.

text.p: The precious metals were reluctant to leave narrow price bands during European trading on Friday, although market sentiment tended to be bearish in the near term.
Gold prices shrugged off fresh U.S. economic data, while the platinum group metals (PGMs) ignored news of production cuts in key producer Russia, dealers said.
Gold fixed virtually unchanged in the afternoon at $341.40 versus $341.20 in the morning.
Prices had started the day easier after softening late on Thursday in New York, but barely moved since in light volumes.

The market had no immediate reaction to weaker than expected U.S. Producer Price Index data, which boosted Wall Street and reinforced conventional wisdom that the Federal Reserve will not raise interest rates in July.
The May PPI declined by 0.3 percent in May against forecasts of a 0.1 percent increase.
The PGMs were also very quiet, moving in relatively narrow prices bands on light volumes.
News on Friday morning that gas cuts as Russia's Norilsk Nickel were affecting metal output at the flagship combine had no effect on the market, dealers said.
Protracted export delays from Russia, a key producer, have caused extreme supply tightness and rocketing prices in recent weeks. But Russian officials say supplies will resume soon.
"Russian stories have been cropping up with such abundance that people are weary of it. No one is even paying attention any more," a dealer said.
Spot palladium remained very tight, although some liquidity had returned to the PGM market, he added.
It was last quoted at $201.95/206.95, down $6.05 from Thursday's close, after probing the psychological $200 area earlier in the day.
Platinum was last quoted $2.00 lower at $438.00/443.00.
Silver was mirroring gold and was hovering around the $4.70 interim support area.
It was last quoted at $4.69/$4.71, down around six cents from Thursday's close. In case of dips, the previous low of $4.60 would provide support.
